# WP-001: Fix Cron Notification Feedback Loop

## Metadata
- ID: WP-001
- Phase: Dogfood
- Priority: P1
- Estimated complexity: M
- Upstream issue: HKUDS/nanobot#1441

## Problem Statement

When a cron job executes and delivers a notification to a channel (e.g. Telegram),
the notification message is re-ingested by the agent loop as if it were a new user
message. This causes the agent to react to its own output, potentially scheduling
more cron jobs and creating an infinite recursion loop.

The root cause is that outbound cron notifications flow through the same message
processing path as inbound user messages. There is no mechanism to distinguish
between "the system sent this" and "the user sent this."

## Reproduction (from upstream issue #1441)

1. Ask the bot to set a reminder: "Remind me in 10 seconds"
2. Wait for the reminder to fire
3. Observe logs: the reminder text enters _process_message as a "user" message
4. The agent interprets it as a new instruction and may schedule another cron job
5. Infinite loop

Log signature:
  nanobot.cron.service:_execute_job — Cron: executing job
  nanobot.agent.loop:_process_message — Processing message from telegram:user: [cron text]
  nanobot.agent.loop:_run_agent_loop — Tool call: cron({"action": "add", ...})

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Cron job notifications delivered to channels must NOT re-enter the agent loop
   as user messages
2. Existing cron functionality must continue to work (jobs execute, notifications
   deliver when deliver=true)
3. All existing tests pass
4. New tests prove the feedback loop cannot occur:
   - Test that cron execution with deliver=true sends to channel but does not
     trigger _process_message
   - Test that actual user messages still process normally
   - Test that cron execution with deliver=false produces no channel message

## Key Files to Investigate

- nanobot/cron/service.py — _execute_job, the cron execution path
- nanobot/agent/loop.py — _process_message, the message intake path
- nanobot/bus/ — the event bus connecting channels to agent
- nanobot/channels/base.py — channel base class, how messages flow in vs out
- nanobot/cli/commands.py — where cron callbacks are wired up (on_notify)

## Implementation Guidance

The fix likely involves one or more of:
- Tagging outbound messages with a source indicator so the bus/channel can
  distinguish system-originated messages from user-originated messages
- Preventing the channel from publishing cron notifications back onto the
  inbound message bus
- Adding a guard in _process_message that filters messages originating from
  internal systems

The approach should be minimal and not require changes to every channel
implementation. Prefer a solution at the bus or agent loop level.

## Test Strategy

Write tests FIRST (TDD):
1. Unit test: mock cron service executing a job with deliver=true, verify
   the notification reaches the channel send method but does NOT appear
   in agent loop message processing
2. Unit test: verify normal user messages still flow through to _process_message
3. Integration test: simulate the full cron-fire-to-channel path and assert
   no re-entry into the agent loop

## Out of Scope

- Network reconnection handling (mentioned in #1441 as secondary observation)
- Changes to how cron jobs are scheduled via the agent
- Channel-specific fixes (this should be fixed at the framework level)
